note: Captured once from the published effect-dynamodb@1.40.0 and @effect-dynamodb/schema@1.40.0, installed outside the repo and run by a scratch script against DynamoDB Local. Entities Plain, Versioned (versioned: true), Retained (versioned: { retain: true }) and Unique (unique: { byId: ["id"] }) over { id, note: string, counts: Record<string, number>, tags?: Record<string, number> }, counts configured { storedAs: SparseMap(), field: "sr" } and tags { storedAs: SparseMap() }, on DynamoSchema.make({ name: "vt", version: 1 }). Each case puts { id, note: "é", counts: { a: 1 } } (the map whole, as sr), moves the map to its entries (counts#a) where the case says entries, and sends one write of the entry b = 2 with no condition, one that holds (note = "é"), one that doesn't (note = "no"), or one only DynamoDB can tell (size(note) = 1: UTF-16 code units, which DynamoDB Local counts, say 1; UTF-8 bytes 2). For a write that reads the row first, another writer moves something just before the write is sent: nothing, the version (+1), the map to its other form, both, or the map before every write. Recorded: the outcome (a result, or a failure's tag, attributes and the first line of its message), every request it sent, whole and in order, what get read back, and the row after. The table's name is replaced by <table>, UUIDs by <token> and timestamps by <time>. Never regenerate it: it is the record of what 1.40.0 did.
